extraction.name: EuroSAT
extraction.description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images for land use and land cover classification
extraction.creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
extraction.citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2 [cs.CV] 1 Feb 2019
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were downloaded from Sentinel-2A via Amazon S3. Images were selected from European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas, distributed over 34 European countries. Images with low cloud level were selected to improve the chance of getting valuable image patches.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentinel-2A satellite multi-spectral images covering 13 spectral bands from the European Space Agency's Copernicus program, accessed via Amazon S3
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images recorded all over the year from European cities
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Bands with lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted from satellite images. RGB images were computed by combining the red (B04), green (B03) and blue (B02) bands.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times. Mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice were sorted out and corrected. No atmospheric correction was applied to the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Images were labeled into 10 land use and land cover classes based on the European Urban Atlas. Classes were selected based on visibility at 10 meters per pixel resolution and frequency of coverage. All images were manually checked and corrected multiple times.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables applications in agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, and environmental monitoring. It can be used for detecting land use and land cover changes, monitoring deforestation (a main contributor to climate change), and assisting in keeping geographical maps up-to-date.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset aims to cover high intra-class variance by including images from 34 European countries recorded throughout the year. Within classes, different land types are represented. Between classes, there is low positive correlation, with the most common confusions being between agricultural classes and between residential and industrial building classes. The classifier sometimes confuses agricultural land classes as well as highway and river classes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with color cast. A classification system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow finely graduated per-pixel segmentation. The dataset is limited to European geographic coverage and 10 meters per pixel spatial resolution.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation for land use and land cover classification. Applications include land use and land cover change detection, monitoring deforestation, urban area development tracking, nature protection, sustainable development, and assisting in keeping geographical maps (e.g., OpenStreetMap) up-to-date.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We have chosen 10 different land use and land cover classes based on the principle that they showed to be visible at the resolution of 10 meters per pixel and are frequently enough covered by the European Urban Atlas to generate thousands of image patches... rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: With access to such data, applications in the domains of agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, or environmental monitoring can be realized... For instance, deforestation is a main contributor to climate change, therefore the detection of deforested land is of particular interest (e.g., to notice illegal clearing of forests).

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We aimed for the objective to cover as many countries as possible in the EuroSAT dataset in order to cover the high intra-class variance inherent to remotely sensed images... Between the classes, there is a low positive correlation. The classes most common to each other are the two presented agricultural classes and the two classes representing residential and industrial buildings... It is shown that the classifier sometimes confuses the agricultural land classes as well as the classes highway and river.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Please note, the proposed dataset has not received atmospheric correction. This can result in images with a color cast... While a classification system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow a finely graduated per-pixel segmentation...

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The proposed dataset can be leveraged for multiple real-world Earth observation applications. Possible applications are land use and land cover change detection or the improvement of geographical maps... The presented examples are particularly of interest in urban area development, nature protection or sustainable development.
